question.text: Yamuna VC Fund (Cat I) has invested in a seed-stage deep-tech startup with no revenue, no profit, and two uncertain go/no-go milestones 18 months out. Per IPEV 2022, the most appropriate primary valuation technique is:

answer.text: Milestone/scenario analysis; the Option Pricing Method (OPM) may also be used
Mandatory use of replacement cost only

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per PDF Section 11.8.3 point 2: 'Many seed, start-up or early-stage investments are valued using a milestone approach, or scenario analysis. ... the option pricing method (OPM) is also used sometimes.' DCF is inappropriate because cash flows cannot be reliably forecast; EV/EBITDA fails when EBITDA is negative. **The Trap:** DCF is too speculative pre-revenue; EV/EBITDA requires positive EBITDA; replacement cost is too narrow. IPEV specifically flags milestone/scenario/OPM for this stage. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same. XV (Research Analyst) tests real-options / OPM valuation with more mathematical depth. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For seed-stage investees, document the specific milestones (tech, regulatory, customer) and probability-weight them in the valuation memo. This becomes your anchor for the mark-to-market at each valuation date — LPs expect this rigour in the fund's annual LP letter.
